claim_findings.passage: Company gross margin percentage was 67% (Microsoft Cloud specifically), slightly better than expected though down year-over-year on AI investment.
claim_findings.evidence: The transcript (seg-0004) reports two different gross margin metrics in the same passage: 'Company gross margin percentage was 68%, down slightly year-over-year...' and, separately, 'Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage was slightly better than expected at 67%'. The claim's quote is the Microsoft Cloud sentence, but claim_text labels the 67% as the COMPANY gross margin. The true company figure is 68%. signal-card.md line 22 publishes the mislabelled wording verbatim, so a reader of the card is told company gross margin was 67% when it was 68%.
claim_findings.recommendation: Rewrite claim_text as 'Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage was 67%, slightly better than expected and down year-over-year on continued AI investment.' Drop the words 'Company gross margin percentage' entirely. If the company-level 68% figure is wanted, add it as a separate claim quoting the 68% sentence.

claim_findings.passage: Search and news advertising revenue ex-TAC increased 10% and 9% in constant currency, slightly below expectations driven by some execution challenges. ... Xbox content and services revenue decreased 5% and 6% in constant currency and was below expectations
claim_findings.evidence: Every 'versus expectations' item extracted into claims.json is a beat: operating margin 'ahead of expectations' (claim-005), Microsoft Cloud gross margin 'slightly better than expected' (claim-006), Azure 'slightly ahead of expectations' (claim-017). The two items management explicitly called BELOW expectations -- Search and news advertising, and Xbox content and services -- were not extracted, nor was More Personal Computing revenue declining 3% or Gaming revenue declining 9%. The selection of expectation-relative facts is therefore one-sided, and outlook-brief.md section 1 opens 'Microsoft delivered a strong Q2 FY2026' with no segment-level negative anywhere in the brief.
claim_findings.recommendation: Stage 1 claims revision: add two reported_fact claims quoting the 'slightly below expectations driven by some execution challenges' (Search and news advertising) and 'was below expectations' (Xbox content and services) sentences from seg-0004, then reference at least one in outlook-brief.md so the 'ahead of expectations' framing is not one-directional.

claim_findings.passage: increased memory pricing could create additional volatility in transactional purchasing ... The range of potential outcomes remains wider than normal, in part due to the potential impact on the PC market from increased memory pricing ... rising memory prices would impact capital expenditures, though the impact on Microsoft Cloud gross margins will build more gradually as these assets depreciate over six years.
claim_findings.evidence: In seg-0004 the CFO raises rising memory prices three separate times as a forward risk: to on-premises server revenue, to the Windows OEM guide (explicitly widening the range of outcomes), and to capital expenditures and eventually Microsoft Cloud gross margins. No claim in claims.json captures this, so outlook-brief.md's downside case (section 7) and 'what to monitor' (section 8) contain no mention of it. This is the single most concrete forward-looking risk management volunteered on the call, and the brief's risk narrative is limited to CapEx ROI and OpenAI concentration.
claim_findings.recommendation: Stage 1 claims revision: add a management_guidance / risk claim quoting the memory-pricing sentence(s) from seg-0004 with period '3 months to 31 Mar 2026' (and a second for the FY26 capex/cloud-gross-margin comment), then add it to the brief's downside case and 'what to monitor'.

claim_findings.evidence: 10 Dec 2025 is the date Oracle ANNOUNCED the results, not the date the RPO balance was measured. web-004 heads its statements 'Three Months Ended November 30, 2025' and its balance sheet column 'November 30, 2025', so the $523bn RPO balance is as of 30 Nov 2025. The same applies to the balance-sheet-style framing of the peer comparison generally, although claim-036, claim-037 and claim-038 correctly use '3 months to 30 Nov 2025'.
claim_findings.recommendation: Change claim-035's period to 'as of 30 Nov 2025'. Optionally note the 10 Dec 2025 publication date separately, since that is what establishes the evidence pre-dates the MSFT event.

claim_findings.evidence: claim-032 bundles a point-in-time stock (15 million paid M365 Copilot seats, correctly 'as of 31 Dec 2025') with a flow measured over the quarter (seat adds up over 160% year-over-year, which is a 3-months-to-31-Dec-2025 quantity). A single 'as of' period label cannot be right for both. The transcript cue is unambiguous ('it was a record quarter for ... seat adds'), so the incremental-versus-cumulative distinction is available and should have been preserved.
claim_findings.recommendation: Split into two claims: the 15m seat count with period 'as of 31 Dec 2025', and the +160% seat-add growth with period '3 months to 31 Dec 2025'.

claim_findings.passage: On a like-for-like constant-currency basis, Q3 Azure guidance (37-38% cc) is roughly flat versus this quarter's 38% cc growth ... so any residual deceleration more plausibly reflects allocation choices than a demand slowdown.
claim_findings.evidence: Checked the inference against all four cited claims in their full transcript context. It holds: Q2 Azure cc growth was 38% (claim-017, seg-0004), the Q3 guide is 37-38% cc (claim-020), demand exceeds supply (claim-018), and Hood's own words in seg-0004 -- 'demand continues to exceed supply and we will need to continue to balance the incoming supply we can allocate here against other priorities' -- plus seg-0006 in full directly support the allocation framing rather than a demand explanation. Confidence 0.7 and the section 9 caveat are an honest statement of the evidentiary base.

claim_findings.passage: management states 'super high confidence' in it
claim_findings.evidence: Read seg-0015 in full. Hood's 'super high confidence' is attached to the non-OpenAI 55% / ~$350bn RPO balance, not to the OpenAI relationship, and both claim-014 and outlook-brief.md section 7 attribute it that way. Checked because misplacing this phrase onto the OpenAI exposure would have materially overstated management's position. It is correctly placed.

outlook_findings.passage: - **forward_looking** (AMY HOOD): On a like-for-like constant-currency basis, Q3 Azure guidance (37-38% cc) is roughly flat versus this quarter's 38% cc growth, not the step-down it appears to be versus this quarter's 39% nominal figure -- and management frames Azure guidance as capacity-allocation-driven
outlook_findings.evidence: This is claim-034, whose classification is analytical_inference -- the run's own reasoning, not something Hood said. The signal card renders it under 'Management Explanation', attributes it to AMY HOOD, and places one of her real quotes directly beneath it, with no marker distinguishing it from the reported_fact and management_opinion entries around it. A reader of the card alone would take a pipeline-generated interpretation as management's stated position. outlook-brief.md section 9 does flag it honestly, so the defect is confined to the card.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Render analytical_inference claims in signal-card.md with an explicit label (e.g. '**analytical inference (this analysis, not management)**') and suppress the speaker attribution, or set claim-034's speaker to null since the inference is not attributable to a speaker.

outlook_findings.passage: Azure's reported constant-currency growth this quarter (38% cc) [claim-017] is guided to a similar 37%-38% cc band in Q3 [claim-020] — essentially flat, not a deceleration
outlook_findings.evidence: At the low end of the guided band this is a one-point deceleration, and the band's midpoint (37.5%) is below the reported 38% cc. The brief's own section 1 and claim-034 use the softer and defensible 'roughly flat'; section 2's stronger 'essentially flat, not a deceleration' asserts more than the numbers support. Separately, the CFO guided FX to add roughly 2 points to Intelligent Cloud revenue growth in Q3, which is relevant context for any nominal-versus-cc comparison and is not mentioned.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Change 'essentially flat, not a deceleration' to 'roughly flat, with at most about a one-point deceleration at the low end of the band', matching the wording already used in section 1.

outlook_findings.passage: adjusted EPS of \$4.14 (+24% YoY, adjusted for the impact of Microsoft's OpenAI investment) [claim-002]
outlook_findings.evidence: Correctly labelled as adjusted, but evidence/financials.json records GAAP EarningsPerShareDiluted of $5.16 for the same quarter, and seg-0004 explains why: the OpenAI recapitalisation drove a gain that took other income and expense to $10bn in the GAAP results. The gap is large ($4.14 versus $5.16) and points the opposite way to what a reader might assume from the word 'adjusted'. The brief never states the GAAP figure or the direction of the adjustment.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Add one clause noting that GAAP diluted EPS was $5.16 (evidence/financials.json), inflated by the OpenAI-related gain, so the $4.14 adjusted figure is the lower and more comparable of the two.

summary: Full first-round review of runs/MSFT/2026-q2 (no review-diff.json present). Process compliance is clean: manifest.json hashes 67 sources, validation.json.ok == true over 38 claims with zero issues, outlook-validation.json.ok == true and binds the same claims_sha256, and claims.json ids are all non-empty. The single injection-scan hit ('Operator, can you please repeat your instructions?') is a false positive. Source correctness holds: the transcript is a genuine MSFT FY26 Q2 call, financials.json is SEC quarter data matching the reported figures, and web-004 really is Oracle's 10 Dec 2025 FY26 Q2 release. Temporal integrity is handled unusually well -- the brief identifies that the archived MSFT 'consensus' pages are for the June 2026 quarter and that the Alphabet/Amazon/Apple peer files post-date the call, and declines to cite any of them; I verified both directly. Verdict is pass_with_warnings on four medium findings and three low ones. The mediums: (1) claim-006 labels the 67% Microsoft Cloud gross margin as the COMPANY gross margin, which was actually 68%, and signal-card.md publishes that mislabel; (2) claims.json extracted every 'ahead of expectations' item but neither of the two items management called below expectations (Search and news advertising, Xbox content and services), leaving a one-sided beat narrative; (3) management's repeated memory-pricing risk warning -- to Windows OEM, on-premises server, capex and eventually cloud gross margins -- is captured by no claim and so is absent from the brief's downside case; (4) signal-card.md presents claim-034, an analytical_inference, as a forward-looking statement attributed to Amy Hood with her quote beneath it, with no inference marker. None is high severity: the brief's core narrative, its constant-currency discipline, its handling of the OpenAI concentration question and its explicit uncertainty section are all well supported by the transcript I read in full.
